claim_1.claim: ELISpot analysis of fresh PBMC from 24 healthy BCG-vaccinated adults at screening and 1, 2, 4, 12 and 24 weeks post-vaccination showed both intradermal and intramuscular MVA85A induced high Ag85A-specific IFNγ responses peaking at day 7 and remaining significantly above baseline at week 24, with no significant difference between intradermal and intramuscular groups.

sources.quote: IFNγ ELISpot assays were performed on freshly isolated PBMC from all 24 subjects at screening and at 1, 2, 4, 12 and 24 weeks post-vaccination

Both intradermal and intramuscular MVA85A induced high levels of Ag85A-specific IFNγ at the peak (day 7) time-point. The responses were durable, staying significantly above baseline six months post-vaccination (Wilcoxon matched pairs test).

The median antigen-specific IFNγ response in the intradermal group exceeded that of the intramuscular group (Fig. 3) but this difference did not reach statistical significance at any time-point. An AUC analysis of the response summed over six months showed no difference between the two groups (p = 0.62, Mann Whitney U test).

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of cryopreserved PBMC from vaccinated subjects at weeks 0, 1 and 24 showed both intradermal and intramuscular MVA85A induced significant PPD- and 85A-specific CD4+ T-cell production of IFNγ, TNFα and IL2, including polyfunctional CD4+ T cells, compared to baseline, with no significant differences between vaccination routes at any time-point.

sources.quote: Mycobacteria-specific cytokines (IFNγ, TNFα and IL2) were measured in subjects’ cryopreserved PBMC after overnight stimulation with PPD and a single pool of 85A peptides (Fig. 4). Both routes of vaccination induced significant IFNγ, TNFα and IL2 at weeks 1 and 24 post vaccination. Levels of produced cytokines between the two groups did not significantly differ at any time-point.

claim_3.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of unstimulated cryopreserved PBMC from 4 subjects at weeks 0, 1 and 2 showed substantial CD4+ T-cell expression of CCR4, CCR6, CCR7 and CXCR3 in both intradermal and intramuscular groups, with no significant differences between routes.

sources.quote: The effect of vaccination route on cell trafficking was evaluated by measurement of CD4+ T cell surface expression of chemokine receptors CCR4, CCR6, CCR7 and CXCR3. This was initially performed in both mycobacteria-stimulated and unstimulated cells for 4 subjects.
Fig. 4D shows median expression of these chemokine markers in unstimulated cells. Substantial levels of expression were detected in both groups, which were not significantly different.

claim_4.claim: ELISA analysis of serum from 12 intramuscular and 12 intradermal vaccinees at weeks 0, 2, 4 and 24 showed intradermal MVA85A significantly increased anti-85A IgG at week 4 and week 24 compared to baseline and week 2, whereas the intramuscular group showed no significant increase and there were no significant differences between groups at any time-point.

sources.quote: Anti-r85A IgG was measured in serum samples collected at week 0, 2, 4 and 24.

Volunteers who were vaccinated intradermally with MVA85A had significantly higher serum IgG 4 weeks post-vaccination when compared to baseline (p = 0.0342) and week-2 (p = 0.0005). There was no significant increase during follow-up in IgG levels in the intramuscularly immunised group, similarly no significant differences were observed between the two groups at any of the time points.
